notes.uncertainty: Each card quotes its standard error and a 95% interval of the statistic over the selected events; below N = 15 the interval is shown beside the SE, with the card's small-sample caveats.
notes.showers: Showers A and B are reported separately, each with its own N; an event without shower-A hits has no A prediction and is dropped from A, never zero-filled.

model.title: Incident Angle Estimation Model
model.caption: The angle network of the absolute (detector) frame predicts each shower's polar angle θ (angle_absolute_pred) against the incident θ; the azimuth φ is not predicted. θ does not wrap, so its mean residual is a meaningful bias. The headline is the θ resolution per shower, in mrad.

rmse.label: RMSE
rmse.interval: square root of the 95% Student-t interval of the mean squared residual, from N ≥ 2

mae.label: MAE
mae.interval: 95% Student-t interval of the mean absolute residual, clipped at 0, from N ≥ 2

median_rel.label: Median relative error
median_rel.interval: 95% percentile bootstrap of the median (B = 2,000, seeded per series, bin and quantity) from N ≥ 20; exact order-statistic interval from N ≥ 6

bias.label: Bias
bias.interval: 95% Student-t interval of the mean residual, from N ≥ 2

median_abs.label: Median absolute error
median_abs.interval: 95% percentile bootstrap of the median (B = 2,000, seeded per series, bin and quantity) from N ≥ 20; exact order-statistic interval from N ≥ 6

bootstrap.seed_rule: numpy SeedSequence([42, frame, shower, bin, quantity]): frame is the position in lab, trans, local, shower 0 for A and 1 for B, bin the producer's momentum-bin number, quantity the position in rmse, mae, median_rel, bias, median_abs
bootstrap.sampler: order statistics of the resample drawn exactly through Beta variates; the same distribution as resampling the bin

notes.showers: Showers A and B are separate series, each with its own N. A shower without a prediction (an event with none of that shower's hits) is counted per bin in n_missing and dropped, never zero-filled.
notes.own_bin: Each shower is placed in its own momentum bin: shower A by e1_bin and shower B by e2_bin, because the two showers of an event carry two momenta. The bins are the producer's integer column over the whole dataset, so the axis does not move with the selection.
notes.frames: One response carries every input frame the networks were trained in (absolute, the legacy per-shower translated frame, and local), so one task can be compared across frames on a single axis.
notes.calibration: The networks predict the momentum scale directly; no sampling-fraction calibration is applied.
notes.whiskers: Every whisker is the 95% interval of the aggregate it sits on (its interval is named in quantities), never the dispersion of the showers in the bin. A bin of one shower has a value and no whisker, and the median has none below N = 6, because none can be estimated there without assuming a distribution.
notes.scale: A point drives the y range from N = 15. Under-powered points above it are clipped, with their true values in y_max.overflow; with no driving point the range is provisional, set by point values only, and any whisker beyond it is clipped and listed likewise.
notes.angle: The angle network predicts the polar angle θ only, so there is no azimuth residual and nothing to wrap. Residuals are in mrad. A relative error |Δθ| / θ grows like 1 / θ at small θ, so each point also carries the median |Δθ| in mrad, the smallest true θ in the bin (rad) and the number of showers with θ < 0.1 rad.
